hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y with positive steady-state gain.
With u=0 the reservoir drains on its own so y decays toward a low equilibrium.
Response has short lag/delay of a few seconds and settles over tens of seconds, not instantly.
There is no large dead-zone: u >= 0.1 produces a detectable rise.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, so a second amplitude will scale proportionally.
Holding target y=0.6 requires a mid-range steady u roughly 0.4-0.7.
Level sensor has moderate zero-mean noise requiring averaging over seconds, not single samples.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Primary gain magnitude and lag/delay: a mid-level long hold separates fast-large vs slow-small response and is required to size control gain and settling allowance.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage: 0.2273 + 0.10*0.3*20 = 0.8273 which stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y rises from ~0.23 with 1-3s lag toward ~0.3-0.5, slope flattening but still >0 over last seconds unless settled; noise visible but mean trend up.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero experiments completed; gain magnitude, lag, drain rate, linearity, hold-input for 0.6, and noise are all unresolved, so no controller can be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: holding low-mid pump to measure rise rate, lag and early gain.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y with positive steady-state gain.
With u=0 the reservoir drains on its own so y decays toward a low equilibrium near zero.
Original response had 2-4s lag/delay and ~10-15s time constant, settling over ~30s, not instantly.
There is no large dead-zone: u >= 0.3 produces detectable inflow versus u=0 drain.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, so a second amplitude will scale proportionally.
Holding target y=0.6 requires steady u ~0.6-0.7, above the u=0.5 equilibrium ~0.44.
Level sensor has moderate zero-mean noise ~+/-0.015 requiring averaging over seconds, not single samples.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller steady rise and slower rise slope even after delay elapsed.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 fall is faster and same u holds a lower level than before.
Change is slower response / longer transport delay (~8-12s vs 2-4s): level keeps following previous command for many seconds after a change, then responds with similar slope.
Change is sensor change: different offset or noise behaviour vs original +/-0.015 zero-mean noise.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Delay length vs gain loss: whether low y after ~8s of u=1 is due to longer dead-time with rise imminent or weaker pump with no imminent rise, which decides between detuning for delay vs raising feedforward gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative rise 0.112+0.10*1.0*7.0=0.812 stays below soft limit 0.85 with 0.038 margin, assuming no drainage and no lag; level starts low and no in-transit command exceeds 1.0.
proposal.expected_observation: If longer ~8-12s delay is right, y at ~0.11 after ~8s of u=1 will start rising within 2-4s, ending ~0.18-0.30 with last-5s mean clearly above start and slope >0.015/s; if purely weaker gain with short delay, y would stay <0.15 with slope ~0-0.005/s and no sharp break.
proposal.readiness_justification: Original gain direction, drain, noise and feedforward are resolved, but change type is not: delay is suggested by after-change trace yet no controlled after-change hold has isolated dead-time from gain/outflow, so redesigning now is unsafe and one short hold is acceptable.
proposal.operator_note: Holding full pump 7s from low level to watch for delayed rise.
